analysis.summary: A refactor of the internal email retrieval logic introduces type mismatches and nested arrays in email recipient fields, which will cause AWS SES runtime validation failures.

bugs.title: Nested array in email recipient fields causes SES validation failure
bugs.description: The function 'getInternalEmail' was changed to return a string array (string[]), but 'createEmailRequest' and 'createEmailRequestWithMultipleRecipients' still wrap its return value in another array (e.g., [internalEmail]), resulting in a nested array structure [['email1', 'email2']].
bugs.risk: AWS SES SDK (and most email libraries) expects a flat array of strings (string[]) for the 'To' and 'Bcc' fields. Providing a nested array ([string[]]) will cause a runtime validation error, preventing any emails from being sent in non-production environments or when BCCing the archive in production.

bugs.title: Type mismatch in email recipient assignment
bugs.description: In 'createEmailRequest', the variable 'to' (declared as a string via the function parameter) is assigned the value of 'internalEmail' (which is now string[]).
bugs.risk: In a non-production environment, this assignment causes the 'to' field to contain an array object instead of a string. When this is later wrapped in '[to]' at line 86, it creates the nested array structure that will crash the SES send call.

notBugs.reason: The addition of a default ISO string for signature timestamps in manualUploadedDocumentAttributes is a functional requirement to ensure data completeness when a document is manually marked as completed.
The use of 'new Set([...])' to remove duplicates in the combined email path is a safe and intended logic change to avoid redundant recipients.
Moving ALD customer IDs to configuration while maintaining a hardcoded fallback is a standard migration pattern and not a bug.
